paragraphs: The M4 Competition has been part of the M4 range since 2014, spanning two generations under one badge. Early cars (F82/F83, 2014 to 2020) use the S55 — a 3.0-litre twin-turbo inline-six derived from the N55, shared with the M2 Competition, M3 and M4 of that era. From 2021, the G82/G83-generation M4 Competition switched to the S58, a newer twin-turbo inline-six that's a genuine reliability improvement over its predecessor — with a closed-deck block and well-proven B58 architecture. The S58 is a different unit entirely, not an evolution of the S55. The F82/F83 M4 Competition is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre twin-turbo inline-six fitted to the M4 Competition from 2014 to 2020 across two chassis codes (F82 coupe, F83 convertible). Known for crank hub failure under hard use — see the callout above. We replace the crank hub with an upgraded unit, along with timing chain components and bearings, as standard on every S55 rebuild.

A genuinely different design from the S55, with no known significant defect pattern confirmed — it's a genuine reliability improvement over the previous-generation S55 with a closed-deck block and well-proven B58 architecture.

compatibility.intro: Because the M4 Competition spans two distinct engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an S55 part will work on an S58 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:
